rows.proof: `DEBT REPAYMENT SCHEDULE JUNE 30, 2015`, PDF pages 42-43 of the FY2015 annual town report -- ONE table across two pages, SIXTEEN debt issues against 32 fiscal years FY2016-FY2047 plus a TOTAL column. THE COLUMNS ARE NAMED FROM THE PRINTED HEADER, NOT INFERRED: the `FISCAL YEAR` stub row carries its own four-digit year per column and each was read -- page 42 runs FY2032 at top=41.8 down to FY2016 at top=581, page 43 carries TOTAL at top=38.9 and FY2047 at 79.7 down to FY2033 at 502+. Increasing `top` is right-to-left on the printed page. THE ROW GRID IS THE PAGE'S OWN ROW LABELS, read and written down: each issue is a block of four printed rows -- the issue name, then PRINCIPAL, INTEREST and TOTAL -- which gives 51 row anchors on each page (16 issues x 3, plus GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL, GRAND TOTAL INTEREST and TOTAL DEBT). Both pages carry the same 51 anchors and the same sixteen issues in the same printed order, checked name by name. FIVE OF THE SIXTEEN ISSUES PRINT THE IDENTICAL NAME `MUNICIPAL PURPOSE`, and that is why the first reading of these pages held TWELVE issues rather than sixteen: keyed on the printed name, the five collapsed into one and the later figures silently overwrote the earlier, which made the row sums nonsense (a `MUNICIPAL PURPOSE` principal row summing to $1,420,000 against a printed TOTAL of $400,000). THE KEY HERE IS THE ISSUE'S PRINTED POSITION, 01 to 16, as well as its name. A printed label is not a unique identifier and nothing on this page says it is. THIS FILE IS THE YEAR DETAIL: one row per (issue, fiscal year), with the principal, the interest and the total the page prints in that year for that issue. 32 year columns x 16 issues; every cell the page prints and nothing it does not. The TOTAL column is NOT here -- it is `fy2015-p42-debt-issue-totals.csv` -- so that no figure is transcribed twice. WHAT PROVES IT: 237 of the 238 printed (issue, year) rows close EXACTLY on principal + interest = total, to the dollar, with no tolerance. The one row that does not is MASS WATER POOL 9* in FY2024, which prints a principal of $418,704 and NO interest and NO total at all -- so nothing asserts it, and the verifier names it rather than scoring it either way. That blank is not ours: it is the final payment year of that issue, and it is the whole explanation of the $418,704 attested on the issue-totals file. A SECOND, INDEPENDENT CHECK, computed across this file and the grand-total file: for 89 of 96 (year x measure) assertions, the printed GRAND TOTAL equals the sum of the FOURTEEN NON-MS-HS ISSUES exactly, to the dollar. The seven that miss are FY2016 and FY2017 interest and total at -$1 and FY2020 interest and total at +$1, and PRINCIPAL -- the one measure printed without cents underneath -- ties EXACTLY in all 32 years. That contrast is what says displayed rounding rather than a bad read, and it is why no tolerance is declared on the row identity, which closes to the dollar regardless. THE TOWN'S GRAND TOTAL ROWS EXCLUDE THE TWO MS-HS CONSTRUCTION ISSUES FROM EVERY YEAR COLUMN, AND THAT IS NOW ESTABLISHED ARITHMETICALLY RATHER THAN BY EYE. In each of the thirty year columns where they pay, $9,000,000 and $20,605,000 of MS-HS CONSTRUCTION are left out of GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL, GRAND TOTAL INTEREST and TOTAL DEBT: FY2033's printed grand total principal is $82,050, which is MUNICIPAL PURPOSE SEWER $49,018 plus MUNICIPAL PURPOSE WATER $33,032 and leaves out the $320,000 and $730,000 printed two rows above it. The TOTAL column of those same three rows DOES include them -- its $49,556,201 of principal is the sum of all sixteen issues -- and page 41's `Total Long-Term Indebtedness` prints $49,556,203 for 2015 with $29,605,000 of Schools debt outside the general debt limit, which is those two issues together. $29,605,000 is exactly the difference between the 32 printed year columns of GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL ($19,951,201) and the TOTAL cell of the same row ($49,556,201). WHAT FOLLOWS FOR A READER: the town's published per-year forward debt service for FY2016 onward understates its own total by the school construction debt, $29.6M of the $49.6M outstanding. WHAT IT DOES NOT SHOW: why the two issues are excluded. Debt outside the general debt limit is a real statutory category and page 41 reports it separately, which fits, but nothing on either page states that this is the reason and nothing here tests it. THE PER-ISSUE ROWS ARE COMPLETE AND ARE WHAT SHOULD BE USED.

Increasing `top` is right-to-left on the printed page. Both pages carry the same 51 anchors and the same sixteen issues in the same printed order, checked name by name. FIVE OF THE SIXTEEN ISSUES PRINT THE IDENTICAL NAME `MUNICIPAL PURPOSE`, and that is why the first reading of these pages held TWELVE issues rather than sixteen: keyed on the printed name, the five collapsed into one and the later figures silently overwrote the earlier, which made the row sums nonsense (a `MUNICIPAL PURPOSE` principal row summing to $1,420,000 against a printed TOTAL of $400,000). THE KEY HERE IS THE ISSUE'S PRINTED POSITION, 01 to 16, as well as its name. A printed label is not a unique identifier and nothing on this page says it is. THIS FILE IS THE TOTAL COLUMN, printed on page 43: what each of the sixteen issues owes in principal, interest and total over the whole of FY2016-FY2047. The year-by-year detail is `fy2015-p42-debt-by-issue.csv` and no figure is in both. WHAT PROVES IT: the sixteen rows sum, in the principal column, to the $49,556,201 the page's own GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL row prints in its TOTAL cell, and in the interest column to the printed $23,200,767 -- both EXACTLY, to the dollar. Fifteen of the sixteen rows also close on principal + interest = total. THE ONE THAT DOES NOT IS THE TOWN'S ARITHMETIC, AND IT IS NOW FULLY EXPLAINED. MASS WATER POOL 9* prints principal $3,373,156, interest $700,555 and total $3,655,007, which is $418,704 BELOW its own two components. $418,704 is exactly the FY2024 principal of that same issue -- its final payment year -- and page 42 prints NO total cell for MASS WATER POOL 9* in FY2024. So this row's TOTAL is footed on the printed YEAR TOTALS, of which FY2024's is blank, rather than on its own principal and interest. The 32 printed year totals of that row sum to $3,655,007 exactly, which is what confirms it. THE SAME $418,704 CARRIES INTO THE PAGE'S OWN GRAND TOTAL: the sixteen rows sum to $72,338,264 in the total column against a printed TOTAL DEBT of $72,756,968, a difference of exactly $418,704 in the same direction. So the town's grand total is consistent with principal plus interest and this one row is not, and the figure the document omits is identified rather than merely measured. WHAT IT DOES NOT SHOW: whether the blank FY2024 total cell is a typesetting omission or a deliberate statement about that payment. Nothing on either page distinguishes them, and no tolerance is or could be declared for a $418,704 difference -- it is named, not absorbed. -- closes: the Treasurer's own FY2015 debt service schedule, which is not published.

THE PAGES ARE MIRRORED AND ROTATED IN THEIR OWN TEXT LAYER, like page 34: the words read backwards and what scans as a row at constant `top` is a COLUMN, so every word is reversed and the table is transposed before anything is read. No recognition is involved. THE YEAR COLUMNS ARE NAMED FROM THE PRINTED HEADER, NOT INFERRED: each `top` band carries its own four-digit year label, read and checked -- page 42 runs FY2032 at top=42 down to FY2016 at top=581, page 43 carries TOTAL at top=41 and FY2047 at 80 down to FY2033 at 573. Increasing `top` is right-to-left on the printed page. THE ROW GRID IS THE PAGE'S OWN ROW LABELS: every row prints PRINCIPAL, INTEREST or TOTAL, which gives 51 row anchors on each page -- 16 issues x 3 rows, plus GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL, GRAND TOTAL INTEREST and TOTAL DEBT -- and the two pages carry the same 16 issues in the same order, matched by name. THIS FILE IS THE THREE PRINTED GRAND TOTAL ROWS, one row per fiscal year, exactly as the page prints them. Each year closes on its own: grand total principal plus grand total interest is total debt, 32 of 32 years, to the dollar. WHAT DOES NOT CLOSE IS THE DOCUMENT, and all three columns are attested rather than tolerated: the 32 printed years of GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL add to $19,951,201 against the $49,556,201 the same row prints in its TOTAL cell, and the $29,605,000 between them is EXACTLY the two MS-HS CONSTRUCTION issues -- and exactly the `Schools` figure page 41 prints outside the general debt limit. The interest row is short $17,755,661 against those issues' printed interest totals of $5,195,300 and $12,560,362, a dollar apart because of the same $5 the detail file attests. THE DOCUMENT'S OWN GRAND TOTAL ROWS ARE INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT, AND THIS IS THE FINDING OF THE PAGE. In every one of the thirty year columns where they pay, the two MS-HS CONSTRUCTION issues ($9,000,000 and $20,605,000) are EXCLUDED from GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL, GRAND TOTAL INTEREST and TOTAL DEBT -- the printed FY2033 grand total principal is $82,050, which is exactly MUNICIPAL PURPOSE SEWER $49,018 plus MUNICIPAL PURPOSE WATER $33,032 and leaves out MS-HS $320,000 and $730,000 printed two rows above it. THIS WAS CHECKED BY EYE, NOT INFERRED: page 43 was rendered and looked at, and the grand total rows are printed in blue beneath the MS-HS blocks with those columns visibly blank of them. WHAT FOLLOWS FOR A READER: the town's published per-year forward debt service for FY2016 onward understates the town's own total by the school construction debt, which is $29.6M of the $49.6M outstanding. The per-ISSUE rows are complete and are what should be used.

rows.proof: `FY 2016 Omnibus Budget`, PDF pages 140-141 of the FY2015 annual town report -- the appropriations the town voted, 91 printed lines numbered 1 to 82 with nine letter suffixes (3A, 3B, 13A, 14A, 43A, 61A, 71A, 79A, 79B), in twelve named sections. THE TABLE IS SET AS TWO PANELS PER PAGE AND IT IS ONE LIST, READ COLUMN-MAJOR: the left panel of p140 carries lines 1-31, its right panel 32-58, p141's left panel 59-73 and its right panel 74-82. The line numbers run strictly upward through all 91 rows in that order, which is what settles the pairing -- reading ACROSS the printed line instead pairs line 23 `Town Accountant` with `Total Protection`, and that is the error this geometry makes most easily. WHAT PROVES IT: the 91 line items sum to $32,025,895.00, which is the TOTAL OMNIBUS the page itself prints at the foot of p141, EXACTLY, to the dollar. The twelve section totals the pages print ALSO sum to the same figure exactly, and each section's own lines sum to its own printed total -- twelve further assertions, all closing to the dollar, none of which the grand total alone would have caught. LINE 62 `Town Highway Garage $1,020.00` IS THE WHOLE OF THE OMNIBUS RESIDUAL. The generic extract of these pages was short by exactly $1,020 on $32.0M, and the row is printed plainly on p141: the figure was lost because the two panels' baselines differ by less than the banding tolerance, so it landed in a panel with no label. It is already recorded in `table-corrections.csv` (appropriations/2015/141/62, read, 2026-09-28) and this transcription confirms it by eye on the page's own bitmap. `$ -` IS AN EXPLICIT ZERO AND IS TRANSCRIBED AS 0.00, not as a missing figure: every one of the 91 rows prints a `$`, and nine of them print a dash after it (lines 3, 3B, 14A, 18, 27, 51, 57, 61A, 79A, 81). Reading a dash as absent is what turned an FY2014 line into a section heading and dropped $16,687,431. EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT (line 47) IS INSIDE `Subtotal Other Protection`, THOUGH IT IS PRINTED ABOVE IT WITH A BLANK LINE EITHER SIDE. Lines 48-53 alone sum to $183,993 against a printed subtotal of $190,493, and the $6,500 difference is exactly line 47. That is established by the arithmetic, not by the layout, which reads the other way. AND THE TWO PANEL HEADINGS DISAGREE ABOUT THE YEAR. The table is titled `FY 2016 Omnibus Budget`; its RIGHT panel on p140 is headed `VOTED FY 2016` and its LEFT panel `VOTED FY 2015`. WHAT THE DATA SHOWS: one continuously numbered list, one TOTAL OMNIBUS, and two column headings naming different years. WHAT IT DOES NOT SHOW: which heading is the misprint, from these two pages alone. A reader who takes the left panel as FY2015 figures and the right as FY2016 would be reading one vote as two.

rows.proof: THE WAGE AND SALARY SCHEDULE, PDF page 198 of the FY2015 annual town report: 20 GRADES against STEP 1 to STEP 8, in HOURLY RATES of pay -- not salaries and not an appropriation. THE COLUMNS ARE NAMED FROM THE PRINTED HEADER, which reads `Grade | Step 1 | Step 2 | ... | Step 8` in white on black across the top of the grid. THE PAGE PRINTS NO TOTAL ANYWHERE and nothing on it adds to anything, so there is NO arithmetic to close. It is checked on the shape the grid asserts about itself, which is weaker than arithmetic and says so: a misread digit survives it untouched. What is declared is that EVERY ONE OF THE 20 ROWS CARRIES EXACTLY 8 FIGURES -- the printed header says how wide a row is, and a row that came out seven cells long is a rate lost -- and that the GRADE never goes backwards through all 160 cells. 160 of 160 cells are transcribed, with no cell blank anywhere on the grid. A REGULARITY WAS TESTED AND REFUSED AS A CHECK. The steps sit about 3% apart and it is tempting to use that as the arithmetic the page lacks; `round(step_1 x 1.03^(n-1))` does not reproduce the grid, so publishing it would be a hypothesis dressed as a proof. The same test failed on FY2022's schedule for the same reason. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW: what anybody was paid. A rate table is a schedule of rates, not a payroll -- it says nothing about hours, headcount, which grade any post sits in, or which fund pays it. The job titles and their grades are printed as PROSE on this same page and are not transcribed here.
